sylvinite_varieties_fabric | Red sylvinite (e.g. seam КрII): distinct layering; halopelite layers 1–2 mm; rich sylvinite layers 1–5 cm with up to 95% sylvite, grains 0.5–1.5 mm. Banded sylvinite (seam А): thinner layers, higher sylvinite/halite ratio — richest, KCl often >50%. Variegated sylvinite (carnallite-pack seams, e.g. Б): layered and massive varieties; milky-white sylvite owes colour to numerous tiny gas bubbles and halite micro-inclusions 0.001–0.1 mm; grains 3–5 mm (to 1 cm); massive variety giant-crystalline (>1 cm, often 2–3 cm), clay-anhydrite inclusions 1–5 mm.
notes: Gas-bearing milky sylvite links to gas content / outburst hazard (Ch.2.9, 3.7).

tectonic setting — Pre-Ural foredeep boundaries | Pre-Ural foredeep = large syncline transitional from Russian platform to folded Urals; deeper pre-Kungurian strata and Kungurian salts. W boundary south of Kosva river = steep (1–5°) basement step + gravity gradient zone = Krasnoufimsk fault; in the Solikamsk depression no such step in Kungurian/Artinskian, W boundary drawn conventionally (thickness/facies of Lower Permian), gradient zone lies 10–15 km further east. E boundary = appearance of Lower Permian molasse [232, 270], near Artinskian outcrops (Nyrob, Krasnovishersk, Vsevolodo-Vilva, Chusovoy) [270].

regional faults I–III | Krasnoufimsk (I): gravity gradient zone + steep (≤5°) step of Artinskian top S of Solikamsk depression; late-Paleozoic deep fault [232]; Artinskian reefs and change to thick sulphate Kungurian section; less distinct within the Solikamsk depression but drawn north to fault III. West-Uralian (II): basement crush zone of en-echelon deep faults ~20 km wide (gravity, magnetics, Sverdlovsk DSS profile), east of the West-Ural fold front → thrust structure; regional thrusts bound E edge of Lower-Permian flysch-molasse. Predtimansky (III): boundary of Belomorian/Karelian massifs [270]; SW boundary of Cherdyn suture zone [232]; NW landscape lineament of Poletaev [119].

description: structural complex II (sylvinite pack) fold distribution | Within salt uplifts sylvinite seams are complexly folded: folds up to 1–3 m (single seams) and up to 20–30 m (whole complex). Most intense (overturned, continuous) at uplift crests and next to rock-salt replacement zones; on flanks folded zones 50–200 m wide alternate with calm areas 100–250 m wide. Upper seams more deformed; upward folds more asymmetric, higher, narrower. Comb-like asymmetric swells of seams especially typical of the Solikamsk uplift. Interseam rock salt less deformed. Faults rare: reverse faults/thrusts 15–20 cm to 1–3 m.
notes: zone widths 50–200 / 100–250 m and Solikamsk-uplift comb swells are new; relevant for heterogeneity/anisotropy of SKRU-1 host seams

rhythmic layered texture of salts | Salt rocks have rhythmic-layered texture; the repeating element is termed annual rhythm [292], layer [297,332] or set [93]; lateral layering generally very persistent. Red sylvinite annual layer per Vakhrameeva [39]: 5 sublayers bottom-up (clay-anhydrite; coarse-medium feathery halite; sylvinite; fine halite; one row of halite crystals); Khodkova [33,326] recognizes as sedimentary only halopelite, matte-white feathery halite and sealing-wax-red sylvite sublayers, others epigenetic (solution migration).

texture evolution during replacement | Stages of texture evolution during replacement by rock salt: (1) initial - layering preserved, clay-anhydrite interlayers continuous, red sylvinite replaced by spar halite within interlayers (Fig 2.38, layer 5 KrII BKPRU-2), short fractures filled by secondary minerals (2.39); (2) breaks in clay-anhydrite interlayers, spar-halite block boundaries crossing several annual layers -> layered-block texture (2.40); (3) anhydrite cores: massive/spotty texture, sometimes brecciated anhydrite (2.41-2.43). Carnallite->variegated sylvinite transitions keep weaker layering; massive texture patches inside variegated sylvinite fields.

primary vs secondary minerals | Poikilitic structures with primary-generation host minerals (dark-grey feathery halite, brownish-red sylvite of red/banded sylvinites, meat-red carnallite) are not typical; secondary minerals (red/pink halite, milky-white sylvite) typically host inclusions. Replacement structures: in sylvinite pack sylvite fully replaced by brownish-pink halite (pseudomorphs); in carnallite pack carnallite replaced by milky-white or brownish-red fine sylvite and halite. Structures reflect a continuous metasomatic process: reaction (initial) -> poikilitic/relict (middle) -> full replacement/metamorphs (final).

description: gas_content_classification | §2.9 Gas content: gases are free vs bound [175]. replacement_zones_genesis_problem | §3.4: The role of epigenesis in VKM reduces historically to genesis of пестрые сильвиниты and rock salt of replacement zones (зоны замещения): open-basin (primary) vs buried-deposit (secondary) schools. Dynamometamorphism hypothesis (Morachevsky [184,185], Razumovskaya [247]): carnallite → sylvinite under tectonic pressure, MgCl2 brine squeezed out. Morachevsky's facts: identical seam structure regardless of lithology; пестрый сильвинит in most folded places/periphery of seams; thinner sylvinite parts; massive coarse texture; blue halite, milky-white sylvite; high gas saturation. Author's criticisms: пестрый сильвинит often in calm bedding while strongly crumpled seams are often carnallite; no experiments; carnallite water insufficient (brine would need 46.85% MgCl2).

Author: cross-cutting contacts exist and are not tectonic (§2.2); zonal crystals are rare; hypothesis fails to explain giant-crystalline texture, gas saturation of milky-white sylvite, blue halite, why lower boundary of пестрый сильвинит of seam Б strictly coincides with the roof of seam А. By 1954 most salt geologists accepted primary (facies) origin of replacement zones [84].
